subject.title: Skipped group messages behind requireMention do not reach message hooks, which blocks full-history archive plugins

question: Should installed plugins be allowed to passively observe messages skipped by `requireMention` before agent/session dispatch, and if so must that visibility be behind an explicit operator or plugin access gate?
rationale: This changes the public Plugin SDK privacy boundary by exposing conversation content that current routing intentionally keeps out of public hooks and agent sessions.

options.title: Gate Observation Before Merge
options.body: Add an explicit operator/plugin access gate for skipped-message observation, then land the public hook once the contract and tests prove the boundary.

options.title: Approve Installed-Plugin Trust
options.body: Accept that installed plugins may observe skipped inbound messages without a separate gate, but record that approval visibly before merge.

options.title: Keep Internal Ingest Only
options.body: Reject the public hook for now and document that full-fidelity archive plugins require internal hooks or channel-specific owner work.

recommendation.title: Gate Observation Before Merge
recommendation.body: Add an explicit operator/plugin access gate for skipped-message observation, then land the public hook once the contract and tests prove the boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent mention-policy and hook/routing work makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the product/security decision.
